data.name: Gaureeshankar
data.gender_notes: Gaureeshankar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gaureeshankar is a compound name derived from two words: 'Gaur' and 'Ishankar'. Gaur refers to 'God' or 'Lord' and Ishankar refers to 'Lord Shankara', who is a manifestation of Lord Shiva. Thus, Gaureeshankar signifies the 'God of Auspiciousness'. The name Gaureeshankar carries the meaning “God of Auspiciousness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gaureeshankar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of auspiciousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of divine blessings and prosperity.
data.etymology: Gaureeshankar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Auspiciousness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gaureeshankar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gaureeshankar holds great significance in Hindu culture, particularly in regions where Lord Shiva is revered. It is evocative of the deep devotion and reverence towards Lord Shiva as the giver of prosperity and good fortune. The use of this name reflects a desire for divine protection, blessings, and the spirit of auspiciousness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Gaureeshankar signifies the quintessential embodiment of the divine presence. It is a reminder of the ultimate reality that is beyond the material world and instills a deep sense of devotion, surrender, and self-realization. The name evokes a sense of peace, contentment, and a connection to the divine, fostering inner growth and spiritual evolution.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gaureeshankar: The name Gaureeshankar symbolizes the supreme God Shiva, residing in the heart of the universe (Gaura) and bestowing blessings of prosperity and wisdom (Eeshankar).

historical_references.reference: Gaureeshankar is believed to be the name of a Hindu god, Lord Shiva, in the ancient Indian state of Bengal. Gaureeshankar is mentioned in the Shiva Purana, a religious text composed between 5th and 6th centuries CE. In this text, Gaureeshankar is described as the presiding deity of the Gaura region in Bengal.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Gaureeshankar can be found in the 17th century Bengali text, 'Brahmanda Purana'. In this text, Gaureeshankar is described as the protector of the universe and the ruler of the Trijana (the three worlds). He is also described as being located at the center of the universe, symbolized by the 'Meru Mountain'.
